name: Mass partition problem
description: The problem of, given a fixed family P of partitions of R^d each splitting it into a fixed number of parts and a family H of measures, deciding whether some partition in P splits each measure in a prescribed way.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Absolutely continuous finite measure (mass partition setting)
description: A finite Borel measure on R^d that is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, so that every hyperplane has measure zero.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: General position (point set)
description: A finite set of points in R^d such that no d+1 of them lie on a common hyperplane.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Ham Sandwich theorem
description: Given d finite measures absolutely continuous w.r.t. Lebesgue measure on R^d, there is a single hyperplane that simultaneously bisects every one of them.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Borsuk-Ulam theorem
description: Any continuous odd map f from the d-sphere S^d to R^d (satisfying f(x) = -f(-x)) has a zero.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Dold's theorem (equivariant map nonexistence)
description: For a finite group G of order >1, if X is n-connected with a free G-action and Y is paracompact of dimension at most n with a free G-action, then there is no G-equivariant continuous map X to Y.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Test map / configuration space scheme
description: A method reducing a combinatorial mass-partition problem to the nonexistence of a G-equivariant map by parametrizing partitions as a configuration space X, encoding the splitting via a test map f to a space Y carrying a G-action.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Necklace splitting theorem (Hobby-Rice / Alon)
description: For m absolutely continuous probability measures on R and r thieves, there is a partition using (r-1)m cuts whose pieces can be distributed among r parties so each receives an equal share of every measure.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Moment curve lifting (necklace splitting proof)
description: Embedding measures on R via the moment curve t -> (t, t^2, ..., t^m) into R^m and applying the Ham Sandwich theorem, so a bisecting hyperplane yields the required cuts.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Grünbaum-Hadwiger-Ramos problem
description: The problem of determining the smallest dimension d for which a single arrangement of k hyperplanes can equipart any given collection of j measures in R^d.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Nandakumar-Ramana-Rao problem
description: The question of whether any convex body (or measure) in R^d can be partitioned into k convex pieces that are simultaneously equal in measure and in a prescribed list of d-1 additional continuous functionals (e.g. perimeter).
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Convex equipartition theorem (spicy chicken theorem)
description: For k a prime power, any absolutely continuous probability measure on R^d admits a partition into k convex pieces of equal measure on which any chosen d-1 continuous functionals are also equalized.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Holmsen-Kynčl-Valculescu conjecture
description: A conjecture asserting bounds on partitions of colored point sets into parts each capturing prescribed numbers of points from each color class while respecting a containment/transversal condition.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Center Transversal theorem
description: For any k+1 measures in R^d there exists a k-dimensional affine subspace that is a center transversal, meaning every hyperplane containing it has at least a 1/(d-k+1) fraction of each measure on each side.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Yao-Yao partition theorem
description: A measure in R^d can be partitioned into 2^d convex cones from a common apex, each of equal measure and with bounded directional spread, enabling efficient geometric range searching.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Same-type lemma
description: Given finitely many point sets in general position in R^d, large positive-fraction subsets can be chosen so that every transversal choosing one point per subset realizes the same order type.
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: PPA-completeness of discrete Ham Sandwich
description: Computing a discrete ham sandwich cut, with dimension as part of the input, is complete for the complexity class PPA (Polynomial Parity Argument).
source_article: A survey of mass partitions, Edgardo Roldán-Pensado and Pablo Soberón, 2022 (BAMS 59(2))

name: Jones polynomial
description: A Laurent-polynomial invariant J(L) of an oriented link L, determined uniquely by a skein relation together with the normalization J(unknot)=1.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Kauffman bracket
description: A state-sum invariant of unoriented link diagrams obtained by resolving each crossing into two smoothings, recovering the Jones polynomial after framing correction.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Khovanov homology
description: A bigraded homology H(L) of an oriented link, built from a cube of resolutions using a rank-two Frobenius algebra, whose graded Euler characteristic is the Jones polynomial.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Categorification
description: The process of lifting an algebraic invariant to a richer categorical object (e.g. homology groups or a category) whose decategorification (Euler characteristic or Grothendieck group) recovers the original invariant.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Reduced Khovanov homology
description: A variant of Khovanov homology defined using a marked point on the link, splitting unreduced homology and refining the invariant.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Functoriality of Khovanov homology under link cobordisms
description: A smooth cobordism between links in R^3 x [0,1] induces a (well-defined up to sign) map on Khovanov homology, making it a functor from the link cobordism category.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Lee spectral sequence and Lee homology
description: A deformation of the Khovanov differential yields Lee homology of dimension 2^{#components}, with an induced spectral sequence from Khovanov homology converging to it.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Rasmussen s-invariant
description: An integer s(K) extracted from the adjacent quantum gradings of the two surviving generators on the E-infinity page of the Lee spectral sequence, defining a concordance homomorphism.
dependencies: Lee spectral sequence and Lee homology
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Rasmussen's slice-genus bound
description: The s-invariant is a homomorphism from the smooth concordance group and satisfies |s(K)| <= 2 g_4(K), giving a combinatorial lower bound on the slice genus.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Combinatorial proof of the Milnor conjecture (torus knots)
description: Rasmussen's s-invariant gives s(T_{p,q}) = 2 g_4(T_{p,q}) = (p-1)(q-1), yielding the first gauge-theory-free proof that the slice genus of the (p,q)-torus knot equals (p-1)(q-1)/2.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Khovanov stable homotopy type (Lipshitz-Sarkar spectrum)
description: A stable homotopy refinement (a spectrum) whose cohomology recovers Khovanov homology, carrying Steenrod operations that strictly strengthen the homological invariant.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Odd Khovanov homology
description: An integral variant of Khovanov homology, due to Ozsváth-Rasmussen-Szabó, that lifts the Ozsváth-Szabó spectral sequence to Z-coefficients and is mutation invariant.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Kronheimer-Mrowka unknot detection
description: Via a spectral sequence from a singular-instanton homology to Khovanov homology, if reduced Khovanov homology of K has rank one then K is the unknot.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Symplectic Khovanov homology
description: A Floer-theoretic (Lagrangian intersection) construction of a link invariant, defined via the geometry of nilpotent slices, conjecturally and in cases provably isomorphic to combinatorial Khovanov homology.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Spectral sequences from gauge/Floer theories to Khovanov homology
description: A family of spectral sequences from Khovanov homology to instanton, monopole, or Heegaard Floer invariants used to prove detection results in the spirit of unknot detection.
source_article: Categorical lifting of the Jones polynomial: a survey, Mikhail Khovanov and Robert Lipshitz, 2023 (BAMS 60(4))

name: Teichmüller curve
description: An algebraic curve V isometrically and holomorphically immersed in the moduli space M_g of genus-g Riemann surfaces with respect to the Teichmüller metric, i.e. a totally geodesic complex curve.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Holomorphic 1-form / translation surface (X, omega)
description: A compact Riemann surface X with a nonzero holomorphic 1-form omega, equivalently a flat metric |omega| with cone-angle singularities at the zeros of omega, giving a translation structure.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Stratum of abelian differentials
description: The subvariety of the bundle Omega M_g of holomorphic 1-forms consisting of forms whose zeros have a fixed multiplicity partition, preserved by the SL_2(R) action.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: SL_2(R) action on Omega M_g
description: The action of SL_2(R) on the moduli space of holomorphic 1-forms by post-composition with linear maps on the flat charts, leaving each stratum invariant and projecting to complex geodesics in M_g.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, omega)
description: The group of derivatives of affine automorphisms of a translation surface (X, omega); when it is a lattice in SL_2(R) the surface is a lattice (Veech) surface generating a Teichmüller curve.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Primitive Teichmüller curve
description: A Teichmüller curve in M_g that does not arise by covering constructions from a Teichmüller curve in a moduli space of lower genus.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Veech dichotomy
description: On a lattice (Veech) surface, every direction is either completely periodic (the surface decomposes into cylinders of closed geodesics) or every geodesic in that direction is uniformly distributed.
dependencies: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, omega)
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Optimal dynamics of billiards in lattice polygons
description: Billiards in a polygon whose unfolding generates a lattice surface have optimal dynamics: every trajectory is either periodic or uniformly distributed; in particular this holds for regular polygons.
dependencies: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, omega)
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Regular polygons generate primitive Teichmüller curves
description: The translation surface obtained by unfolding billiards in a regular n-gon has a lattice Veech group and generates a primitive Teichmüller curve.
dependencies: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, omega)
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Masur's criterion
description: If the Teichmüller geodesic ray generated by (X, omega) does not return to a compact set infinitely often (its horizontal foliation diverges in moduli space), then the horizontal foliation fails to be uniquely ergodic; conversely recurrence forces unique ergodicity.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Cylinder decomposition and parabolic affine automorphisms
description: Decomposing a translation surface into parallel cylinders with commensurable moduli and applying simultaneous Dehn twists to produce parabolic elements of the Veech group, certifying that it is a lattice.
dependencies: Veech group / lattice surface SL(X, omega)
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Weierstrass curve W_D (genus 2 classification)
description: For each non-square discriminant D, the locus W_D in M_2 of genus-2 surfaces with a double-zero 1-form whose Jacobian admits real multiplication by the order of discriminant D, forming an infinite series of primitive Teichmüller curves.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Classification of primitive Teichmüller curves in genus 2
description: Every primitive Teichmüller curve in M_2 is one of the Weierstrass curves W_D (with the decagon example a special case), giving a complete classification in genus 2.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Finiteness of primitive Teichmüller curves in genus 3 outside W_D
description: In M_3 there are only finitely many primitive Teichmüller curves not belonging to the Weierstrass series W_D.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Infinitude of primitive Teichmüller curves in higher genus (open problem)
description: The open question of whether there exist infinitely many primitive Teichmüller curves in M_g for g >= 5, where no infinite construction is currently known.
source_article: Billiards and Teichmüller curves, Curtis T. McMullen, 2023 (BAMS 60(2))

name: Slice knot
description: A knot K in S^3 that bounds a smoothly embedded disk in the 4-ball B^4.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: Slice genus
description: The minimal genus of a smooth, compact, oriented, connected surface embedded in the 4-ball with boundary the knot K; slice knots are exactly those of slice genus zero.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: Knot mutation
description: The operation of excising a tangle from a knot diagram and regluing it after a rotation, relating the Conway knot to the Kinoshita-Terasaka knot and preserving many invariants.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: Knot trace X(K)
description: The 4-manifold obtained from the 4-ball by attaching a 0-framed 2-handle along the knot K in S^3 = boundary of B^4.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: The Conway knot is not slice
description: Piccirillo's theorem that the Conway knot does not bound a smooth disk in the 4-ball, settling the last sub-13-crossing knot whose sliceness was unknown.
dependencies: trace invariants from knot Floer homology
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: Trace embedding lemma
description: A knot K is slice if and only if its trace X(K) embeds smoothly in S^4, so that sliceness depends only on the diffeomorphism type of the trace.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: Handle-rearrangement construction of trace-equivalent knots
description: Building the knot trace from a 4-ball plus a 1-handle and two 2-handles and reinterpreting which 2-handle is the attaching knot, producing a different knot K' with the same trace as a given knot.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: Trace invariance of nu (knot Floer slice obstruction)
description: The slice obstruction nu coming from knot Floer homology is an invariant of the knot trace, so knots sharing a trace have equal nu, allowing K' to obstruct sliceness of the Conway knot.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: Alexander polynomial
description: A Laurent-polynomial knot invariant Delta(t) giving a lower bound on the genus and invariant under mutation; it equals 1 for both the Conway and Kinoshita-Terasaka knots.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))

name: Vanishing of classical slice obstructions for the Conway knot
description: The fact that every classical sliceness obstruction (Alexander polynomial, signature, Rasmussen s-invariant, etc.) vanishes for the Conway knot, motivating Piccirillo's trace-based approach.
source_article: Getting a handle on the Conway knot, Jennifer Hom, 2022 (BAMS 59(1))
